main_results.result: Added a forward-only superseding CLOSE/replay layer. Existing no-contract historical and schema-v1 runtime-provenance histories are replayed under their frozen bindings; new schema-v2 replay_authorized_v1 histories require the new v2 auditor/registry binding.

Injected mixed-history replay and cross-version selection matrix passed. A separate torn-tail harness exercised 1,613 nonempty partial cuts of a replay-v3 CLOSE frame with zero cases becoming a reporting row; each remained an active unresolved block with torn-tail status.

validated_contracts: Historical/no-contract ADMIT may replay the historical compliance binding and the already-durable current-v1 compliance binding, matching the previously accepted history classes.
Schema-v1 ADMIT may replay only the already-durable current-v1 compliance binding; historical/legacy downgrade is rejected by v3.

A valid schema-v2 replay_authorized_v1 ADMIT may use only the new replay-v3 binding whose authority names auditor-v2 blob b74465bd5f68882cee4c5b3fbd2a98d73a684b81 and registry-v2 blob c4d0439dba3ddf2183835c3fbaa3b3012ec1f468.

Schema-v2 replay-authorized ADMIT -> current-v1 or historical CLOSE is fail-closed; historical/schema-v1 -> replay-v3 CLOSE is fail-closed; invalid/unknown schema-v2 -> replay-v3 CLOSE is fail-closed.
prepare_close is forward-only: it generates a CLOSE only for a recognized replay_authorized_v1 ADMIT and injects registry-v2 into auditor-v2.
A partial replay-v3 CLOSE frame is not scientific evidence in the injected torn-tail model; no partial cut produced a closed reporting row.
measurement_validity_rules: Runtime-provenance version selection is fixed by ADMIT before scoring and by the exact reporting binding at CLOSE; recovery never upgrades or downgrades a durable block based on whichever runtime happens to be current later.
A legacy/non-compliance CLOSE is not a safe fallback for a runtime-contracted ADMIT because it would bypass the pre-score provenance predicate.
Replay authorization is still not a determinism proof. CLOSE/replay versioning only preserves which pre-score authorization predicate governed the attempt.
Torn-tail handling is part of evidence validity: only a complete durable CLOSE can add a reporting row.

incident.detail: An unintended branch named x was created during this invocation by selecting create_branch instead of the intended file-write action. The branch points to frozen SHA 89237fa724851070b8be1fdcf35ce7adc7e20059, was not used for semantic work or file writes, and did not alter main. Config6 forbids such branch/ref probe mutations. No additional out-of-bound mutation was attempted as cleanup; the incident is carried explicitly for audit.

scope_limitations: The mixed-history and torn-tail execution harnesses used injected contract-faithful test doubles rather than the full byte-materialized sibling graph.
The persisted v3 Git blob was read back through the connector but has not yet been downloaded and byte-executed as that exact blob in the local Python runtime.
No active/default ProcessStableRuntime was switched to schema-v2 replay authorization; FAIL_CLOSED remains the safe active path.
No trusted deterministic LLM/scorer certificate has been established in this run.
frontier: Materialize blob 99c74f7134210d88cc4cfd0ab857fdd197f7e626 together with the exact frozen sibling graph and byte-execute mixed historical/current-v1/replay-v3 recovery plus torn-tail/crash-restart cases.

Implement a replay-authorized compliance runtime whose ADMIT contract is registry-v2 replay_authorized_v1, whose RESERVE provenance is the authorization-bound binding, and whose CLOSE path is v3; keep FAIL_CLOSED on the current V3-compatible path.
Only after exact sibling execution, expose a ProcessStableRuntime V4 API that refuses generic DETERMINISTIC_REPLAY and requires the pre-score replay-authorization facade.

Stress fresh-process replay with deterministic and stochastic scorers at the declared protected statistic, proving the certificate gate prevents choose-among-retries rather than merely renaming attempts.
Keep connector capability discovery read-only; do not create/delete/move branches, refs or other out-of-namespace objects while probing capabilities.
exact_next_action: Materialize the persisted v3 CLOSE/replay blob and its exact sibling dependencies into one local test directory without reading any non-evaluation state. Byte-execute a three-history journal (historical, schema-v1, replay_authorized schema-v2), verify exact cross-version rejection, then inject crashes/torn tails around the schema-v2 CLOSE. If that passes, build the replay-authorized top runtime while leaving FAIL_CLOSED unchanged.
